Machine Learning.comment: 35 pages, 13 figures, 12 tables. Software and benchmark package: Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23330544

Machine Learning.title: PRISM: Calibrating Black-Box Judges with Counterfactual Probes
Machine Learning.summary: Large language models are increasingly used as judges to reduce reliance on costly human evaluation, yet their scores can systematically disagree with human judgments. We ask whether responses to an explicitly imposed evaluative bias can help correct a judge's implicit scoring biases. We introduce PRISM (Probe-based Residual Inference of Scoring Misalignment), which holds the evaluated content fixed and measures score changes when attributes are emphasized or de-emphasized. A local sensitivity model motivates representing these responses as a surrogate Jacobian. Ridge regression on human labels learns a correction to the baseline score. The resulting scoring protocol is rubric-free: it uses overall scores without requesting criterion-level ratings. In the main Jev and Sol comparisons on SummEval summarization and HANNA story evaluation, PRISM and its learned-baseline variant significantly improve agreement with human rankings over uncalibrated scores while remaining competitive with rubric-based methods. A controlled SummEval comparison yields similar agreement for rubric-derived quality probes and style probes, supporting calibration without reproducing rubric criteria. The learned coefficients reveal shared and opposing correction directions across judges.

Machine Learning.title: Beyond Task Success: A Theory of Representation Reuse
Machine Learning.summary: A learned representation is useful beyond its source task only if later tasks can make use of what the encoder has already learned. Source-task performance, however, gives no guarantee that the representation itself will remain useful once the original head is removed. We study representation reuse with respect to a specified family of future tasks. For such a family, we define the task-relevant state as the coarsest deterministic state sufficient for all of its tasks. A larger task family can require a finer state, and losing a required distinction makes at least one future task unrecoverable on a target support containing that conflict. Exact reuse also depends on how the retained information is presented to the downstream rule. We separate this into structural accessibility, which concerns whether the required distinctions remain recoverable, and coordinate consistency, which concerns whether those distinctions can be interpreted by the same downstream rule across samples. Both failure modes appear separately in the experiments. Reuse improves as task-relevant distinctions become more accessible. Reversible sample-dependent coordinate changes can sharply reduce reuse even when the representation remains recoverable, and inverting the applicable coordinate change restores performance. The same accessibility-reuse ordering appears in prospectively specified CIFAR-100 experiments with both ResNet-18 and DenseNet-121. Finally, preserving a candidate state that contains the distinctions needed by the anticipated task family improves reuse on compatible held-out tasks, with the clearest benefit when target supervision is limited. Representation reuse is therefore relative to the tasks that follow source learning: a useful representation must retain the distinctions those tasks need and make them available in a form that a shared downstream rule can use.

Machine Learning.title: Skin Tone in the Wild: A Dataset and Benchmark for 10-tone MST Classification
Machine Learning.summary: Skin tone classification is a fundamental task in computer vision, with applications in quantifying medical features, assessing demographic representativeness, and mitigating algorithmic bias. However, existing datasets either rely on a restrictive 6-tone Fitzpatrick scale, prohibit training through restrictive licenses, or lack representation of extreme skin tones, while current methods often fail to disentangle true skin tone from in-the-wild imaging conditions, degrading to random-classifier performance. We introduce skin tone in the wild (STW), the first open-access dataset annotated with the 10-tone Monk Skin Tone (MST) scale, containing over 42K images and specifically curated to include underrepresented tones. Alongside a rigorous evaluation protocol, we propose SkinToneNet, a ViT-based model that leverages global image context for robust in-the-wild generalization. Experiments show that SkinToneNet achieves 90% weighted off-by-one accuracy, substantially outperforming prior baselines. We further use SkinToneNet to audit widely used face datasets, including CelebA and VGGFace2, revealing substantial representation imbalances across MST tones.

Machine Learning.title: Selective Successor Eligibility Traces for RLVR
Machine Learning.summary: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has become a key approach for improving the reasoning abilities of large language models. However, widely used critic-free algorithms such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) suffer from coarse-grained temporal credit assignment, as they assign the same trajectory-level advantage to all tokens and fail to distinguish the contributions of different reasoning steps. To address this challenge, we propose Selective Successor Eligibility Traces (S-trace), an critic-free eligibility trace method that enables more effective credit assignment. S-trace introduces successor importance reweighting to recover downstream credit signals under PPO-style clipping and propagates them to selected historical tokens through entropy-based token selection. Theoretically, we establish an upper bound on its discrepancy from the raw eligibility traces-based policy gradient estimator, jointly controlled by the KL divergence and the trace decay factor $λ$. Experiments show that S-trace achieves absolute gains in average pass@16 of 1.80\% and 6.17\% over GRPO, and 2.32\% and 0.87\% over trace-style GRPO($λ$), on Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B, respectively, while maintaining robust gains on Qwen3-8B and producing shorter responses.

Machine Learning.title: Token Utility Is Selection-Conditioned: Coupled Selection of Prompt Context and Response Supervision for Instruction Tuning
Machine Learning.summary: Token selection for instruction tuning is coupled: supervision utility depends on retained context, and vice versa. Existing methods largely optimize prompt compression or response supervision separately. Combining selectors can value supervision using removed context, or context using excluded supervision, creating selection-state mismatch. BRIDGE (Budgeted Response-Prompt Interaction via Directional Gradient-guided Efficient Token Selection) models selection-conditioned token utility through a shared validation-directed surrogate objective. BRIDGE routes response utility to supporting prompt tokens through attention, then alternates budgeted selection to revalue each side under the other's retained subset. Updates reuse precomputed interactions without repeated model scoring, while structure-aware projection promotes coherent supervision spans. Across three model families and three task domains, BRIDGE performs best overall among evaluated selection methods. Its MATH advantage over independent selection grows with compression, reaching 1.66 percentage points on Llama-3.2-3B.

Machine Learning.title: Data-Aware Model Merging in the Essential Subspace for Multi-Task Knowledge Aggregation
Machine Learning.summary: Model merging enables training-free multi-task learning by aggregating knowledge from models fine-tuned from a shared checkpoint, but their task updates can interfere. Using proxy data, we find that task updates induce output shifts whose energy concentrates in a few dominant directions, while many low-energy directions can accumulate across tasks and impair performance. We call the span of the dominant directions the essential subspace. This observation motivates a data-aware framework to preserve essential task knowledge while reducing interference. Essential Subspace Decomposition (ESD) identifies each task's essential subspace from activation shifts measured on proxy data and represents its update compactly while preserving functional behavior. Essential Subspace Merging (ESM) weights each task-update direction by its corresponding output-shift eigenvalue, thereby prioritizing core task knowledge; it then orthogonalizes the weighted directions across tasks to reduce interference. ESM++ extends this merged model by dynamically integrating low-rank task-specific residual experts for adaptive knowledge aggregation. Experiments across diverse task sets and model scales show that ESM and ESM++ effectively aggregate task knowledge while mitigating inter-task interference. Code is available at https://github.com/kiddo127/ESM.

Machine Learning.title: On the Optimality of Random Features under General Conditions: Misspecified Cases and Robust Learning
Machine Learning.summary: Random features provide a standard approach to scaling kernel methods to large datasets by approximating the kernel with a finite-dimensional feature map. Existing works of random feature methods primarily focus on well-specified models and light-tailed noise conditions, leaving a gap in understanding their performance under more general conditions, such as misspecified models and heavy-tailed noise. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive and improved analysis of kernel ridge regression with random features (KRR-RF) under general conditions. In the light-tailed noise setting, we improve upon the worst-case uniform bounds of the feature map used in the previous works and lead to the minimax optimal learning rates with $2r+γ>α_0$, where $(r,γ,α_0)$ denote the regularity of the target function, the effective dimension of the kernel, and the embedding index of the RKHS, respectively. In the heavy-tailed noise setting, we leverage a recently developed Hilbert-valued Fuk-Nagaev inequality and extend the same optimal results under finite weak moment conditions. The additional cost to achieve robustness is a mildly stronger explicit sample-size requirement than in the light-tailed case. For both settings, our results recover the conditions random features budgets (up to log factors) required in the previous works. In the most benign case when $α_0=γ$, KRR-RF are minimax optimal for all $r \in (0,1]$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to establish optimal learning rates for KRR-RF under weak moment conditions in the misspecified setting. Numerical experiments and a real data analysis validate the derived learning rates and demonstrate their practical relevance in the presence of mis-specification and heavy-tailed noise.

Machine Learning.title: From hyperplanes to hyperellipsoids: a pedagogical bridge from linear classifiers to single-qubit mixed-state classifiers
Machine Learning.summary: Quantum machine learning ideas are typically absent from traditional machine learning curricula and are instead introduced in upper-level courses on quantum information processing and quantum computing. We propose a route for bringing quantum ideas into the standard machine learning classroom directly after the introduction of binary linear classifiers. Specifically, we develop a pedagogical bridge between linear classifiers and single-qubit mixed-state classifiers by characterizing their geometric model structure. This characterization reveals that a single-qubit mixed-state model for binary classification can be viewed as the ``ellipsoidal version'' of a standard linear classifier: rather than learning a hyperplane that separates data, the model learns a hyperellipsoid.. We present this connection as an accessible bridge from familiar classical machine learning concepts to quantum machine learning, and encourage instructors to use it as a natural entry point for introducing quantum ideas in the undergraduate machine learning classroom.

Machine Learning.title: Probing the Geometry of Color Representations in Multilingual Language Models
Machine Learning.summary: Do multilingual language models learn a universal internal geometry for color, and is it perceptually grounded or primarily linguistic? We decompose color representations into two geometric axes: (P1) alignment to perceptual color space, and (P2) cross-lingual symmetry. Analyzing layerwise embeddings across models and multilingual datasets, we find that perceptual grounding is weak: alignment to CIE-LAB peaks in intermediate layers, then collapses toward output layers. Cross-lingual symmetry degrades with depth, suggesting later layers encode language-specific structure. Functionally, we show that geometric properties predict task performance: models achieve 96.7% accuracy on color classification at layers where P1 alignment peaks, with P1 alignment (r=0.70) significantly correlating with downstream capabilities. Our results reveal a dissociation: text-only LMs learn universal color-language geometry, not universal color-perception geometry, providing diagnostics for where perceptual structure is preserved in language models.

Machine Learning.title: RCStat: A Statistical Framework for using Relative Contextualization in Transformers
Machine Learning.summary: Identifying which tokens and activations truly influence model predictions is critical for both the efficiency and interpretability of large auto-regressive language models. Yet in practice, token importance is typically inferred from attention distributions that entangle contextual relevance with softmax-normalization effects, obscuring relative influence across tokens and heads. We propose $\textbf{RCStat}$, a statistical framework for quantifying contextual influence in attention mechanisms. At its core $\textbf{Relative Contextualization (RC)}$ is a random variable that measures how strongly one subset of tokens contributes to another under the model's internal scoring scheme. RCStat admits computationally efficient bounds on expected influence that can be estimated at inference time. No retraining is required. We apply RCStat to two tasks. For $\textbf{attribution}$, attention heads with high expected RC accurately identify the prompt spans that drive generation, enabling reliable span-level explanations. For $\textbf{key-value cache eviction}$, RC-based adaptive thresholding selectively evicts low-impact KV entries, substantially reducing cache size while preserving generation quality. Across question answering, summarization, and attribution benchmarks, RCStat achieves consistent gains, improving generation quality by 15-40% with upto 36% error reduction for KV eviction, and attribution accuracy by 2-16%. These results demonstrate that explicitly modeling contextual influence provides a principled and practical alternative to attention-based heuristics.

Machine Learning.title: Over-parameterization Is Neither Robust nor Fragile in Matrix Sensing: A Geometric Theory of Solution Robustness
Machine Learning.summary: Over-parameterization is ubiquitous in modern machine learning, yet its effect on robustness remains poorly understood. We study this question in matrix sensing, a canonical non-convex problem that can also be viewed, under an appropriate parameterization, as training a two-layer quadratic neural network. We develop a rank-aware robustness theory for the Burer-Monteiro factorization when the search rank k may exceed the target rank r_star, thereby capturing over-parameterization. Our analysis shows that robustness depends jointly on the degree of over-parameterization and the local geometry of the attained second-order stationary point: increasing k generally worsens sensitivity, but stationary points with the same search rank can exhibit substantially different robustness. Motivated by this observation, we propose a trajectory-aware algorithm that uses spectral balancing and randomized sketching to steer optimization toward less sensitive solutions. In matrix-sensing experiments, the method reduces paired sensitivity by 18-29 percent for isotropic operators and 87-89 percent for weak-tail operators, without degrading reconstruction accuracy. These results demonstrate that parameter count alone does not determine robustness and identify solution geometry and the optimization trajectory as important levers for improving it.

Machine Learning.title: Tensor-reduced atomic density representations
Machine Learning.summary: Density based representations of atomic environments that are invariant under Euclidean symmetries have become a widely used tool in the machine learning of interatomic potentials, broader data-driven atomistic modelling and the visualisation and analysis of materials datasets.The standard mechanism used to incorporate chemical element information is to create separate densities for each element and form tensor products between them. This leads to a steep scaling in the size of the representation as the number of elements increases. Graph neural networks, which do not explicitly use density representations, escape this scaling by mapping the chemical element information into a fixed dimensional space in a learnable way. We recast this approach as tensor factorisation by exploiting the tensor structure of standard neighbour density based descriptors. In doing so, we form compact tensor-reduced representations whose size does not depend on the number of chemical elements, but remain systematically convergeable and are therefore applicable to a wide range of data analysis and regression tasks.

Machine Learning.title: Inexact calculus of variations on the hyperspherical tangent bundle with connections to the attention mechanism
Machine Learning.summary: We offer a theoretical mathematical background through Lagrangian optimization on the unit hyperspherical manifold and its tangential structure. Our methods can be categorized as inexact since our methods are projection-based and since we will perturb the functional optimization with epsilon-type quantities. We draw connections to the attention mechanism and the Transformer since it exists as a flow map in the tangent fiber for each token along the high-dimensional unit sphere. Our motivation for this work is primarily twofold: we study the attention mechanism under its flow map and its relations to traditional calculus of variations and Lagrangian optimization; and we study several calculus problems of variations on the unit hypersphere that appeal to a broader mathematical lens in approximating, variational contexts.

Machine Learning.title: Do You Even Need More Data? Rethinking LLM Deployment for Label-Scarce Tabular Classification with TabLens
Machine Learning.summary:
Every tabular classification task requires sufficient labeled data. When labels are scarce, practitioners can collect more examples, encode domain expertise into features, or accept lower performance. Large language models offer an alternative by leveraging knowledge acquired during pretraining. This raises three questions: (i) can zero-shot inference reduce the need for labeled data; (ii) can a richer prompt reduce the need for more examples; and (iii) can encoded domain knowledge compensate for missing data? To answer each under explicit, testable conditions, we introduce TabLens, a benchmark of 91 real-world and synthetic datasets across eight domains, plus eight industrial datasets with free-text columns.
  First, below a complexity threshold estimable from a dataset's intrinsic dimensionality before running an LLM, zero-shot inference matches the accuracy of up to about 16 labeled examples. This holds whether the model generates an answer or, more cheaply, scores candidate labels by log-probabilities, which loses almost no accuracy except for the smallest models. Above the threshold, the advantage disappears. On datasets with free-text columns, however, zero-shot LLMs outperform 16-shot TabPFN-3 Plus without manual feature engineering. Second, a richer prompt reduces the number of required demonstrations only when it includes both real column names and a plain-language task description; providing only one can be worse than neither, particularly at higher shot counts. Third, on LLM-synthetic datasets, explicit if--then expert rules help only when the prompt provides enough task context to interpret them, and even then, they substitute for at most about 16 real examples. Together, these results establish testable conditions under which LLMs can reduce data-collection and feature-engineering requirements for tabular classification.

Machine Learning.title: Contextual Representation Flow Across Depth in State-Space and Transformer Architectures
Machine Learning.summary: State Space Models (SSMs) have emerged as efficient, linear-time alternatives to Transformer-Based Models (TBMs) for long-context processing. However, their different mechanisms raise an important question: how does contextual representation flow across depth differ between these model families and their hybrids? We examine this question across twenty-one pretrained models, combining token-wise spectral diversity, layer-wise variation on seven datasets, and answer-location probing on two retrieval tasks. This joint analysis reveals that TBMs retain most of their token diversity at the output, whereas SSMs reach richer intermediate diversity but retain less of it on average, with late-layer compression. Comparisons with reinitialized weights reveal that these profiles depend on pretrained weights, while hybrids combine strong answer-location accessibility with architecture-dependent geometry, showing that high accessibility need not require the steadiest representation flow. Finally, we conduct theoretical case studies connecting these contrasts to mechanism-level differences: query-time token mixing in TBMs, repeated recurrent updates in SSMs, and preserved attention updates in hybrids.

Machine Learning.title: Bayesian Optimization of CVaR with Unknown Hyperparameters
Machine Learning.summary: We study Bayesian optimization of the Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) of an expensive black-box function that depends on a decision and an environmental variable. Existing no-regret algorithms assume that the correct Gaussian process (GP) kernel and its hyperparameters are known. In practice, however, they must be estimated from limited data, often yielding a misspecified surrogate. This is especially damaging for CVaR because misspecification can distort the estimated tail-risk and thus lead to catastrophic decisions. We propose HE-CV-UCB, the first no-regret algorithm for CVaR Bayesian optimization with unknown GP hyperparameters. Given a finite candidate set containing a well-specified model, HE-CV-UCB adaptively eliminates those inconsistent with the observed data, actively queries where the survivors disagree, and returns a design that is robust across the surviving candidates. We prove that it attains cumulative regret matching the oracle rate of CV-UCB up to a factor depending only on the candidate set's size. Across synthetic benchmarks and three real-world applications, HE-CV-UCB achieves competitive performance and frequently outperforms existing CVaR Bayesian optimization methods.

Machine Learning.title: Physically-Induced Atmospheric Adversarial Perturbations: Enhancing Transferability and Robustness in Remote Sensing Image Classification
Machine Learning.summary: Adversarial attacks pose a severe threat to the reliability of deep learning models in remote sensing (RS) image classification. Most existing methods rely on direct pixel-wise perturbations, failing to exploit the inherent atmospheric characteristics of RS imagery or survive real-world image degradations. In this paper, we propose FogFool, a physically plausible adversarial framework that generates fog-based perturbations by iteratively optimizing atmospheric patterns based on Perlin noise. By modeling fog formations with natural, irregular structures, FogFool generates adversarial examples that are not only visually consistent with authentic RS scenes but also deceptive. By leveraging the spatial coherence and mid-to-low-frequency nature of atmospheric phenomena, FogFool embeds adversarial information into structural features shared across diverse architectures. Extensive experiments on two benchmark RS datasets demonstrate that FogFool achieves superior performance: not only does it exceed in white-box settings, but also exhibits exceptional black-box transferability (reaching 83.74% TASR) and robustness against common preprocessing-based defenses such as JPEG compression and filtering. Detailed analyses, including confusion matrices and Class Activation Map (CAM) visualizations, reveal that our atmospheric-driven perturbations induce a universal shift in model attention. These results indicate that FogFool represents a practical, stealthy, and highly persistent threat to RS classification systems, providing a robust benchmark for evaluating model reliability in complex environments.

Machine Learning.title: OctoLong: Mid-Training On Cross-Repository Code Contexts Enhances Long-Context Modeling
Machine Learning.summary: Context lengths of language models (LMs) have dramatically increased, driven by the demands for in-context learning, self-improvement, and long-horizon agentic workflows. However, existing long-context corpora are dominated by books, academic articles, and code repositories, which are finite and often lack long-distance dependencies. In this work, we introduce OctoLong, a context-engineering pipeline that instruments an AST parser, a language server backend, and a package manager to recursively retrieve code references, enabling the curation of dependency-rich code contexts up to millions of tokens long. We then train OctoLong-Instruct, a suite of capable long-context open LMs, derived from base models ranging in size from 600M to 14B parameters, via context-extension mid-training on a approx 50B-token mixture containing approx 6.2B tokens of OctoLong code contexts, followed by approx 10B tokens of instruction tuning. Our ablations and experimental evaluations against 18 strong long-context open-weight LMs show that supplanting just 12% of conventional context-extension corpora with OctoLong data yields substantial gains in long-range retrieval, long-term state tracking, repository-level code understanding, and downstream agentic tasks, while also enhancing API usage in regular coding scenarios.

Machine Learning.title: Learning Shortest Paths with Generative Flow Networks
Machine Learning.summary: In this paper, we present a novel learning framework for finding shortest paths in graphs utilizing Generative Flow Networks (GFlowNets). First, we examine theoretical properties of GFlowNets in non-acyclic environments in relation to shortest paths. We prove that, if the total flow is minimized, forward and backward policies traverse the environment graph exclusively along shortest paths between the initial and terminal states. Building on this result, we reduce shortest-path finding in an arbitrary unweighted graph to finding a non-acyclic GFlowNet with minimal total flow, and approximate it in practice by training with flow regularization. We experimentally demonstrate the performance of our method in pathfinding in permutation environments and in solving Rubik's Cubes of various sizes. For the latter problems, our approach shows competitive results with state-of-the-art machine learning approaches designed specifically for this task in terms of the solution length, while requiring smaller search budget at test-time.

Machine Learning.title: Distribution Matching Evolutionary Algorithms for Rare Event Sampling
Machine Learning.summary: A novel discovery is one which is both useful and surprising: a generative model's output is a useful discovery if it has a low probability of being generated (it's surprising) and a high reward (it's useful). Global optimization can directly increase the probability of sampling high rewards but typically requires updating model weights. Such gradient based optimization is expensive and bars using capable closed-source models. Instead, modern search methods for discovery sacrifice the global target, and use evolutionary algorithms with local reward maximizing objectives, permitting the search to focus only on high probability samples. In this paper, we interpret various evolutionary algorithms as approximate Markov Chain Monte Carlo, an optimization-free method to sample from complex distributions. This interpretation allows developing Distribution Matching Evolutionary Algorithms (DME), a class of search methods which sample from a global target distribution without updating weights. Empirically, DME has a higher sample efficiency than existing methods on problems requiring many samples to find a solution.

Machine Learning.title: Robust Logical Anomaly Detection under Capture Shifts via Synthetic Anomalies
Machine Learning.summary: Detectors of logical anomalies, such as missing, extra or wrongly combined parts, usually score a test image by its distance from normal (good) images. They achieve near-perfect image-level AUROC on standard industrial anomaly detection benchmarks such as MVTec LOCO, but their robustness to changes in capture conditions remains largely unexamined. Under a heterogeneous perturbation protocol in which each test image is randomly kept unaltered or subjected to a brightness reduction or a zoom-out transformation, the normal-reference methods we tested lose 9.7 to 34.1 AUROC points, and two of the strongest, CSAD and SALAD, fall from 97.7% and 96.4% to 68.1% and 62.3%. We propose a framework in which a classifier, trained on normal images and on synthetic anomalies, scores a test image without comparing it with normal data. From a short description of each product, a language model derives anomaly types and editing instructions, an image editor applies them to normal images, and the classifier learns to separate the edited images from automatically discovered normal sub-modes. With its full training recipe, the framework reaches 94.9% AUROC on clean images, 1.5 to 2.8 points below SALAD and CSAD, and 94.1% under the perturbation protocol. Trained without brightness or zoom-out augmentation, so that neither test perturbation occurs in training, it still reaches 92.5% (93.2% clean). These results suggest that clean benchmark scores can hide a strong sensitivity to capture conditions, and that learning the decision from both normal images and rule violations may reduce it.

Machine Learning.title: Which Optimizer Leaks Most? Optimizer Implicit Bias as a Training-Data Privacy Controller
Machine Learning.summary: Releasing a neural network checkpoint can leak information about its training data, and existing reconstruction results rely on gradient-descent training. We ask whether the choice of optimizer affects the ability to recover the training data. Extending work connecting Karush--Kuhn--Tucker conditions to training-data reconstruction, we show that the implicit biases of popular optimizers (SGD, Adam, Muon) leave very different fingerprints of the training data. We argue that the key distinction is the \emph{weight-specificity} of these implicit biases, namely how much continuous information about the final weights the optimizer-dependent target of the stationarity conditions encodes. The limiting stationarity conditions for models trained with SGD and Muon retain enough weight-specific information to reconstruct training examples in practice. For Adam in the $\ell_\infty$ implicit-bias regime, the optimizer-dependent part of these conditions encodes only a discrete pattern of maximal coordinates and their signs, and at nondegenerate KKT points the conditions are too few to identify the training set to first order. Experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 support these claims: models trained with Muon can yield stronger reconstructions at much lower training cost than models trained with SGD, although this advantage depends on the training regime and architecture, and models trained with Adam appear consistently more resistant to the evaluated attacks.

Machine Learning.title: Sim-to-Real Transfer for Muscle-Actuated Robots via Generalized Actuator Networks
Machine Learning.summary: Tendon drives paired with soft muscle actuation enable faster and safer robots while potentially accelerating skill acquisition. Still, these systems are rarely used in practice due to inherent nonlinearities, friction, and hysteresis, which complicate modeling and control. So far, these challenges have hindered policy transfer from simulation to real systems. To bridge this gap, we propose a sim-to-real pipeline that learns a neural network model of this complex actuation and leverages established rigid body simulation for the arm dynamics and interactions with the environment. Our method, called Generalized Actuator Network (GenAN), enables actuation model identification across a wide range of robots by learning directly from joint position trajectories rather than requiring torque sensors. Using GenAN on PAMY2, a tendon-driven robot powered by pneumatic artificial muscles, we successfully deploy dynamic but precise goal-reaching, ball-in-a-cup, and table tennis policies, trained entirely in simulation. To the best of our knowledge, this result constitutes the first successful sim-to-real transfer for a four-degrees-of-freedom muscle-actuated robot arm.

Image and Video Processing.title: Simplifying and Improving On-Policy Distillation for Few-Step Diffusion
Image and Video Processing.summary: Few-step distillation reduces the sampling cost of diffusion and flow models, but existing approaches often require auxiliary score models or specialized architectures. We show that simple on-policy velocity regression already provides a strong foundation for 4-NFE generation. To represent teacher velocity variation within each coarse transition, we introduce Pivot, a training-only residual proxy that separates local corrections from the student's interval-mean prediction. We further repel the student from weaker teacher predictions, providing a lightweight mechanism for avoiding undesirable modes. The resulting framework, Simplified Matching Distillation (SMD), remains entirely regression-based, requires neither online score estimation nor adversarial training, and leaves the deployed generator unchanged. We evaluate SMD on image generation and editing, 3D generation, video synthesis, and joint audio--video generation, scaling to 33 billion parameters. At 4-NFE, SMD outperforms strong few-step baselines and surpasses multi-step teachers on several benchmarks. It also supports cross-model, multi-teacher, and causal-video distillation.

Image and Video Processing.title: Augmenting Real-time Visualization in Minimally Invasive Surgery with Particle Filtering and Depth-Aware Occlusion Handling
Image and Video Processing.summary: We present a real-time, hybrid framework for occlusion handling and depth-aware tracking in minimally invasive surgeries (MIS). Occlusions caused by surgical instruments often obscure the region of interest (ROI), affecting surgical precision. To address this, our approach integrates enhanced You Only Look Once (YOLO) based detection, Particle Filtering (PF), and monocular depth estimation using Multiple Depth Estimation Accuracy with Single Network (MiDaS). Occlusion is detected using a distance-based threshold between instruments and ROI. Experimental results demonstrate robust instrument detection with a confidence score of 0.85, effective occlusion event handling, and accurate depth prediction with an MAE of 0.34 cm and RMSE of 0.53 cm. Independent phantom-based validation against stereo depth measurements yielded an MAE of 0.65 cm and RMSE of 0.66 cm. The framework further achieved an occlusion detection accuracy of 81.95\% while maintaining real-time performance at 38.7 FPS. Preliminary surgeon feedback indicates that the proposed visualization framework is clinically relevant and holds promise for future intraoperative image-guided navigation and decision support in MIS.

Image and Video Processing.title: UEPS: Robust and Efficient MRI Reconstruction
Image and Video Processing.summary: Deep unrolled models (DUM) have become the state-of-the-art for accelerated MRI reconstruction, yet their robustness under domain shift remains a critical barrier to clinical adoption. In this work, we identify coil sensitivity map (CSM) estimation as the primary bottleneck limiting generalization. To address this, we propose UEPS, a novel DUM architecture featuring three key designs: (i) an Unrolled Expanded (UE) design that eliminates CSM dependency by reconstructing each coil independently; (ii) progressive resolution, which leverages k-space-to-image mapping for efficient coarse-to-fine refinement; and (iii) sparse attention tailored to MRI's 1D undersampling nature. These physics-grounded designs enable gains in robustness and computational efficiency. We construct a large-scale zero-shot transfer benchmark comprising 10 out-of-distribution (OOD) test sets spanning diverse clinical shifts, anatomy, view, contrast, vendor, field strength, and coil configurations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UEPS consistently and substantially outperforms existing DUM, end-to-end, diffusion, and untrained methods across all OOD tests, achieving state-of-the-art robustness with low-latency inference suitable for real-time deployment.
Image and Video Processing.comment: The document contains the main paper and additional experimental details in the supplementary material. Open-source code can be found at: https://github.com/HongShangGroup/UEPS

Image and Video Processing.title: Panoramic Out-of-Distribution Segmentation
Image and Video Processing.summary: Panoramic imaging enables capturing 360° images with an ultra-wide Field-of-View (FoV) for dense omnidirectional perception, which is critical to applications such as autonomous driving and augmented reality. However, current panoramic semantic segmentation methods fail to identify outliers, and pinhole out-of-distribution segmentation (pinhole-OoS) models perform unsatisfactorily in the panoramic domain due to pixel distortions and background clutter. To address these issues, we introduce a new task, Panoramic Out-of-Distribution Segmentation (PanOoS), with the aim of achieving comprehensive and safe scene understanding. Furthermore, we propose the first solution, POS, which adapts to the characteristics of panoramic images through text-guided prompt distribution learning. Specifically, POS integrates a disentanglement strategy designed to materialize the cross-domain generalization capability of CLIP. The proposed Prompt-based Restoration Attention (PRA) optimizes semantic decoding by prompt guidance and self-adaptive correction, while Bilevel Prompt Distribution Learning (BPDL) refines the manifold of per-pixel mask embeddings via semantic prototype supervision. Besides, to compensate for the scarcity of PanOoS datasets, we establish two benchmarks: DenseOoS, which features diverse outliers in complex environments, and QuadOoS, captured by a quadruped robot with a panoramic annular lens system. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of POS, with AuPRC increasing and FPR95 decreasing by 34.25 and 21.42 percentage points, respectively, compared with RbA on DenseOoS, outperforming state-of-the-art pinhole-OoS methods. Moreover, POS achieves leading closed-set segmentation capabilities and advances the development of panoramic understanding. Code and datasets will be available at https://github.com/MengfeiD/PanOoS.
Image and Video Processing.comment: Accepted to IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology (TCSVT). Code and datasets will be available at https://github.com/MengfeiD/PanOoS

Image and Video Processing.title: Forecasting Brain Tracer Distribution from Pre-Contrast MRI: A Comparison of Direct Regression and Flow Matching
Image and Video Processing.summary: Intrathecal contrast-enhanced MRI shows how a tracer injected into the cerebrospinal fluid spreads through the brain, but requires repeated scans over 24--48\,h. We therefore ask how much of the later tracer distribution can be predicted from the pre-contrast scan and elapsed time alone. Using 104 training patients (878 MRI volumes), we compared a direct image-to-image regression model with a more complex generative model based on conditional flow matching, and tested both on 23 held-out patients and on 51 patients from a separate cohort with idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (INPH). The direct model reduced the error of simply copying the pre-contrast scan by about 60\% in held-out patients and 25\% in the INPH cohort, and its predicted change maps agreed with the observed tracer enhancement rather than only reproducing anatomy. The generative model was less accurate in both cohorts. A substantial part of the later tracer distribution is therefore predictable from the patient's brain anatomy as seen on pre-contrast MRI, and the added model complexity gave no benefit at this data scale. With prospective validation, such forecasts could be studied for patient stratification and treatment planning in intrathecal therapies.

Image and Video Processing.title: Recovery-Oriented Optical System Design Based on Fisher Information
Image and Video Processing.summary: Traditional optical system design for imaging applications has long been guided by image quality metrics such as geometrical RMS spot size, wavefront error, and modulation transfer function (MTF). Although these metrics effectively characterize direct imaging performance, they do not necessarily indicate optimal behavior when image restoration is subsequently applied. In modern imaging pipelines, however, optical systems are increasingly combined with physics-based or learning-based restoration methods, making the information transfer properties of the optical system critically important. In this work, we propose a recovery-oriented optical design approach that explicitly links optical system optimization with image restoration performance through an estimation-theoretic framework based on Fisher information. A new design criterion is adopted to ensure that the information encoded by the optical system can be reliably recovered during image restoration. To validate the proposed approach, two dual separated aspheric lenses are designed under identical configurations using conventional RMS-based optimization and the proposed recovery-oriented optimization, respectively. Although the RMS-optimized lens exhibits superior direct imaging quality, it underperforms after image restoration compared to the recovery-oriented design. These results demonstrate that recovery-oriented optical design provides a physically interpretable and effective extension of traditional optical design criteria for imaging systems operating within modern computational imaging pipelines.

Image and Video Processing.title: Deficit-Driven Stratified Acquisition for Building STRATA-S12: An Open SAR-Optical Corpus for Self-Supervised Learning
Image and Video Processing.summary: Building a co-registered SAR-optical corpus for self-supervised Earth Observation is above all an acquisition problem, yet the main multi-modal datasets are collected opportunistically, with no per-stratum quota control and no mechanism against the geographic dropout that non-uniform cloud cover leaves behind. We present Deficit-Driven Stratified Acquisition (DDSA), an algorithm that treats building a co-registered Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 corpus as a constrained maximum-coverage problem over a hemisphere-corrected (class x season x region) stratification, enforces strict temporal pairing and a multi-stage quality gate, and closes the loop during acquisition with a human-in-the-loop deficit-repair stage. Measured on its own product, the algorithm yields three results a single-pass acquisition cannot report. Deficit-driven ordering makes a partial run a covering one: it holds every one of the 192 strata populated from the first few percent of the budget, where an abundance-first order leaves most strata empty until the end. Whether a failed attempt can be recovered depends on the temporal persistence of its cause, not the kind of defect: geometric failures such as nodata are among the most repairable (eta = 41.4%) while cloud is among the least (eta = 18.8%), because a cloudy location is cloudy on most dates of its season. The repair loop supplies 39.5% of the released pairs at no measurable quality cost, with 89.8% surviving manual review. The quality guarantee has a price: 2,928,370 acquisition attempts produced 740,746 released pairs. We release the corpus, STRATA-S12, with STAC/PDS4-aligned FAIR sidecars, and a pre-registered linear-probe check confirms it is fit for self-supervised pre-training. A metadata-level coverage comparison against SSL4EO-S12 and SEN12MS situates the corpus over a shared frame; systematic cross-corpus and cross-method comparison is left to follow-up work.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 55 pages. Dataset on Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/datasets/chsanleo/strata-s12 - archived on Zenodo: STRATA-S12 corpus https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22699047 ; reduced subset (D_lite) https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22646276

Image and Video Processing.title: Low-Altitude Agentic Networks: From UAV Connectivity to Workflow-Driven Capability Orchestration
Image and Video Processing.summary: Low-altitude platforms are evolving from connected sensing nodes into autonomous agents capable of bounded task interpretation, skill invocation, and local decision making. Increasing the intelligence of individual unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), however, does not resolve the organization problem that arises when mission workflows depend on capabilities distributed across multiple platforms and provider feasibility changes with network, resource, and mobility conditions. We propose low-altitude agentic networking as a task-level networking paradigm and develop a reference architecture that separates workflow logic from executor identity. Within a validated domain-specific workflow space, each ready operation is translated into a capability requirement and dynamically bound to an agent that remains feasible under current conditions. Task contracts and structured evidence govern workflow execution, while routine provider and link changes are handled through workflow-preserving local adaptation before high-level repair is invoked. A trace-calibrated discrete-event case study identifies a bounded operating region: conventional organization remains effective for simple workflows under stable conditions, whereas agentic networking becomes beneficial when workflow dependencies are tightly coupled, capability feasibility changes during execution, and viable local recovery paths remain available.

Image and Video Processing.title: Background2Background: a self-supervised background removal framework for high dimensional microscopy
Image and Video Processing.summary: High-dimensional microscopy captures features across space, time, and spectrum, but complex backgrounds obscure signals. We present Background2Background (B2B), a self-supervised background removal framework leveraging the backgrounds larger correlation relative to the signal. Local pixel shuffling disrupts signal correlations while preserving background structure, transforming signals into effective noise for Noise2Noise-based background removal. Across fluorescence, stimulated Raman scattering and mid-infrared photothermal imaging, B2B achieves over 40-fold background suppression and reveals hidden signatures.

Image and Video Processing.title: Deep Learning for Atmospheric Turbulence Mitigation: A Comparison Between GANs and Transformers
Image and Video Processing.summary: Atmospheric turbulence creates complex spatial and temporal distortions that significantly reduce image quality. This work compares two deep learning methods for turbulence reduction: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Transformer-based models. Both methods are trained and tested on the SOTIS dataset, which includes multi-frame sequences under different turbulence conditions with ground truth references. Our results show an important finding: GAN-based models perform better in severely degraded, low-quality situations, while Transformer-based models achieve better results in moderate to high-quality settings, especially in correcting geometric distortions. We also enhance the Turbulence Mitigation Transformer (TMT) by introducing a refined training strategy, an augmented input design that includes a temporally averaged frame as prior structural information, and a modified loss function that incorporates the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM). These improvements lead to consistent performance gains across various turbulence conditions. Overall, this study provides an in-depth evaluation of deep learning methods for turbulence reduction and offers practical guidance for selecting models in different imaging environments.
Image and Video Processing.comment: Published in the Journal of Electronic Imaging

Image and Video Processing.title: High-resolution retinal matrix imaging via computational motion and aberration correction
Image and Video Processing.summary: High-resolution optical imaging of the human retina is essential for diagnosing ophthalmic and neurodegenerative diseases. While adaptive optics combined with coherence gating can resolve retinal structures at the cellular scale, it requires complex, costly, and cumbersome hardware to physically correct for ocular aberrations and motion. Matrix imaging offers a powerful digital alternative by leveraging wave linearity to undo aberrations and multiple scattering; however, its in vivo deployment has been hindered by continuous, involuntary eye movements that destroy phase coherence during acquisition. Here, we overcome this fundamental barrier and demonstrate the first in vivo reflection matrix imaging of the human retina using an ultra-simplified optical setup without physical correctors. We introduce a fully computational framework that tracks and compensates for multi-axial ocular motion directly from raw interferometric data, thereby restoring the phase coherence of a multi-spectral distortion matrix. This enables local, high-order aberration correction to achieve diffraction-limited, volumetric imaging of retinal tissues. By shifting the hardware burden to physics-guided numerical computation, this paradigm opens the way for accessible, non-invasive, and high-resolution digital ophthalmology.

Image and Video Processing.title: Per-Bundle, Pre-Reconstruction Inversion for Temporal CT: Flux-Compensation Design and Multi-Patient Generalization
Image and Video Processing.summary: Paper 1 established the per-bundle statistical limits of Temporal CT (TCT) and benchmarked a learned prior on a single patient at a uniform incident count $N_0$. This paper lifts both restrictions. SNN2, a Gauss-Newton estimator, converges to the per-bundle Poisson maximum-likelihood solution and is the prior-free baseline. N$_0$FC, a bow-tie and tube-current-modulation co-design, compresses within-bundle photon-flux dynamic range. V8c is a neural-network residual corrector trained on a 19-patient corpus stratified by water-equivalent diameter (WED). T2bp, a per-patient empirical-Bayes post-processor, combines per-bundle Poisson likelihoods with a prior built from the patient's own bundles; it requires no training, so it cannot inherit a mismatched training prior. Results use Paper 1's bias-charged Dose Inflation Factor (DIF), extended to per-ray budgets. V8c beats SNN2 on in-distribution patients under baseline acquisition but fails out of distribution. Composed with SNN2, T2bp matches or beats T2bp$\circ$V8c on three of four N$_0$FC test cells (WED 207-342 mm), with the largest gains on the high-WED and out-of-distribution patients, and trails by 3% on the fourth. On 23 non-test corpus volumes, N$_0$FC with closed-loop tube-current modulation lowers the per-volume median middle-path Cramer-Rao floor, as a DIF, from 23-48 under baseline acquisition to 3.3-6.3, near the equal-attenuation value 13/3; T2bp$\circ$SNN2 reaches this floor without training, its mean squared error 0.74-1.26 times the floor (median 0.89) over the bulk of each volume. Acquisition co-design removes most of the attenuation-contrast penalty, and a training-free estimator attains the resulting limit. The remaining three- to six-fold gap to dose parity with single-source CT, and the high-attenuation tail, are the target of inter-bundle priors in later work.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 52 pages (29 main text, 23 supplementary material), 7 figures, 14 tables. Paper 2 of a series; companion to arXiv:2604.10934. Preliminary version: the 48-cell corpus results will be recomputed with the truth-free T2bp configuration (see "Note on this version")

Image and Video Processing.title: Perceptual Characterization of Scan-induced Artifacts in Dynamic 3D Meshes
Image and Video Processing.summary: Dynamic meshes reconstructed from real-world scenes often exhibit scan-induced artifacts such as surface jitter and missing geometry, which strongly impact perceived visual quality. Objective assessment remains challenging due to the absence of artifact-free ground truth and limited perceptual understanding of artifact interactions. This paper presents a systematic and controlled perceptual study of scan-induced artifacts in dynamic meshes, focusing on surface jitter and holes. To enable systematic analysis, we introduce a physically grounded artifact synthesis framework in which holes are synthesized using a reconstruction uncertainty model derived from multi-view geometry. The study reveals asymmetric cross-artifact interactions, non-additive integration, and motion-dependent temporal masking. Based on these findings, we propose a compact, perceptually grounded no-reference quality assessment framework that encodes the observed perceptual mechanisms.

Image and Video Processing.title: DoReMe: Dual optimization of Reconstruction and Motion estimation for self-navigated free-breathing abdominal MRI using Gaussian Splatting
Image and Video Processing.summary: Purpose: Free-breathing abdominal MRI is limited by respiratory motion, which introduces image artifacts and k-space inconsistencies. Existing reconstruction approaches often depend on pre-estimated motion fields or external respiratory surrogate signals. We propose a coupled reconstruction-motion estimation algorithm for self-navigated free-breathing acquisition, in which motion is represented by compact Gaussian primitives and jointly refined with the image estimates during iterative reconstruction. Methods: An iterative reconstruction that alternates between data consistency updates and motion modelling was proposed. Respiratory motion was represented using Gaussian primitives. A Gaussian splatting was integrated into the reconstruction algorithm. The method was evaluated on self-navigated free-breathing Cartesian gradient-echo (GRE) acquisition in four healthy volunteers, including retrospective scan shortening experiments, and was compared with regularized compressed sensing (CS) reconstruction. Results: Respiratory motion states were reconstructed in approximately 1.5 min. Compared with CS, the proposed method improved visual image quality, particularly in coronal liver views, and better preserved anatomical structures in retrospectively shortened acquisitions. These findings provide proof of concept for the proposed method. Conclusion: The proposed coupled reconstruction-motion estimation algorithm improved visual image quality compared with CS alone. Gaussian primitives provided a compact and sufficiently flexible representation of nonrigid respiratory motion with practical runtime, supporting further scanner integration and validation in larger cohorts.

Image and Video Processing.title: Focus, Align, and Diffuse: Time-Series-Aware Keyframe Diffusion for Cardiac Dynamic Synthesis from Sparse Observations
Image and Video Processing.summary: Dense cardiac dynamics are essential for assessing cardiac function, yet in practice clinicians often observe only extremely sparse measurements. However, recovering full dynamics from such sparsity is a highly ill-posed problem due to the lack of temporal cues. While auxiliary time-series signals like ECG provide physiological guidance, effectively exploiting them is challenging due to the cross-modal representation gap and phase misalignment. In this work, we present CardioFAD, a Focus--Align--Diffuse paradigm that reformulates sparse cardiac dynamic synthesis as a recoverability--alignability anchor discovery problem. Our core insight is that resolving extreme temporal ambiguity requires a compact set of anchor states that are both sufficient to recover the visual trajectory and reliable for ECG--visual alignment. We therefore learn motion-salient keyframes under two complementary principles: trajectory sufficiency, which preserves trajectory-critical intra-modal motion content, and anchor alignment, which promotes consistent inter-modal correspondence at these anchors. We implement the Focus and Align modules optimized by the two aspects. Diffuse then performs two-stage generation by first synthesizing keyframes and subsequently interpolating the remaining frames. Extensive experiments on cardiac MRI and echocardiography videos demonstrate superior visual quality, temporal coherence, and improved functional consistency under the extreme one-shot regime.

Image and Video Processing.title: Personalising Deformable Image Registration with Clinical Context and Deformation History for Adaptive Radiotherapy
Image and Video Processing.summary: Adaptive radiotherapy must account for anatomical changes during treatment, but doing so depends on reliably mapping targets, organs at risk and dose across serial images. Existing registration methods treat each image pair independently, without using radiotherapy-specific context or the patient's preceding anatomical trajectory. We developed Clinical-context-Aware and Patient-adaptive Deformable Image Registration (CAP-DIR), integrating source contours, dose, clinical text and prior-registration features. We evaluated 16,361 CT examinations from 3,473 patients across four institutional cohorts and five public benchmarks. CAP-DIR increased internal-test organ-at-risk-region normalized cross-correlation from 84.76% to 96.92% relative to the strongest learning-based comparator, with low deformation folding, and remained superior across seven external cohorts. In a blinded review of 20 longitudinal cases, clinically acceptable contours increased from 45.0% to 82.5% for clinical target volumes and from 22.5% to 62.5% for organs at risk, while estimated editing time decreased. In a controlled benchmark, CAP-DIR reduced global dose-mapping error by 34.5% relative to the strongest comparator. These findings show that clinically informed, longitudinal registration can improve contour usability and dose mapping for adaptive radiotherapy.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 27 pages, 7 figures and 6 tables. The submission includes Supplementary Information

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Settling the Approximability of Submodular Facility Location
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: In submodular facility location (SFL), introduced by Svitkina and Tardos (SODA 2006), clients $\cal C$ in a metric space are assigned to facilities $\cal F$. A facility serving a set $S \subseteq \cal C$ of clients incurs cost $g(S)$, where $g$ is a monotone submodular function common to all facilities. The best known approximation factor for SFL is $O(\log\log|\cal C|)$, due to Abbasi, Adamczyk, Bosch-Calvo, Byrka, Grandoni, Sornat, and Tinguely (ICALP 2024), improving on the $O(\log|\cal C|)$-approximation of Svitkina and Tardos. We show that this is best possible up to a constant factor in the value-oracle model by showing that there exists no algorithm with only polynomially many queries to $g$ with approximation ratio $o(\log\log|\cal C|)$. This bound holds for algorithms with unlimited computation time, and when $g$ is restricted to matroid rank functions. We also show that the natural linear programming relaxation has an integrality gap of $Θ(\log\log|\cal C|)$. Our lower bound follows by constructing an extension of Vondrák's symmetry-gap approach (FOCS 2009) for matroid rank functions.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: An initial proof of a constant-factor lower bound was obtained using ChatGPT 6.1 Astra. The stronger result shown in the paper was obtained in conversations with Claude Opus 5.5 and ChatGPT 6.1 Astra. The authors have improved the presentation and simplified the arguments. 25 pages, 2 figures

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Bipartite Matching with Few Rounds of Demand Queries
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We study the randomised and deterministic demand-query complexity of approximate bipartite matching with few query rounds. The demand-query model, introduced in [Blumrosen and Nisan SICOMP 2009; Nisan SODA 2021], is inspired by combinatorial auctions and welfare maximisation, where an oracle returns the first neighbouring vertex (item) of a vertex u (agent) according to a given permutation pi (preference ordering of the agent over the items).
  For randomised algorithms, our main result gives a trade-off between the number of rounds k, the per-round query budget q=n^{1+δ}, and the achievable approximation ratio. Let 1 <= k <= log n, and -1 <= delta <= 1/k. Every k-round randomised algorithm using O(q) demand queries per round has a worst-case expected-size approximation factor of Omega(n^{1/2k-delta/2}/k). Conversely, we give a randomised algorithm achieving approximation factor O(n^{(1-k*delta)/(k+1)}/k) in expectation.
  For deterministic algorithms, for k*q >= n, we show that the optimal deterministic approximation factor is ~Theta(n^2/(q*k^2)), thereby improving the previous lower bound of [Nisan SODA 2021] by a polynomial factor over a wide range of parameters. In particular, for q=Theta(n), we improve the deterministic round-complexity lower bound for constant-factor approximation from ~Omega(n^{1/3}) to ~Omega(sqrt n). Our algorithms produce matching and vertex-cover certificates; the deterministic trade-off also extends to minimum vertex cover and maximum fractional matching.
  We extend the randomised upper bounds to the weaker Demand-OR model [Nisan 2021]. We prove a non-adaptive simulation of uniform random-neighbour queries using known techniques, avoiding the O(log n)-round penalty of the trivial binary-search simulation. Consequently, our upper bounds yield the same k-round approximation guarantees using O(q * log^2 n) Demand-OR queries per round.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Two Holes Make a Difference: Deterministic Paging with Delay and Deadlines
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
In this paper, we study online paging with delay or deadlines. In online paging with delay, an online algorithm manages a cache of size $k$ and needs to serve incoming requests by adding the requested pages to the cache. In addition, it has the option to delay serving incoming requests at a cost that depends on the delay. We propose a new online algorithm, which combines a threshold rule with first-in, first-out (FIFO) replacement, and show that it is $(2k+2)$-competitive for cache size $k$. This result corrects a previously published claim that the competitive ratio is exactly $2k+1$ regardless of the number of holes (pages outside the cache). However, in the case of one hole, we show that the FIFO rule with a different threshold is indeed $(2k+1)$-competitive, giving a tight result.
  In the case of deadlines, the same analysis gives a deadline-triggered algorithm that is $(k+1)$-competitive in general and $k$-competitive if there is only one hole. Moreover, we show that the second hole makes paging with deadlines strictly harder than classical paging, where the competitive ratio is independent of the number of holes. For paging with deadlines, we prove a deterministic lower bound of $k+\tfrac12$, already for two holes. We show that, as a consequence, no threshold-triggered algorithm can achieve a competitive ratio less than $2k+\frac32$ in general.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Policy Iteration Is Not Strongly Polynomial for Deterministic Markov Decision Processes: The Price of Algorithmic Anarchy
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We establish exponential iteration lower bounds in the number of states for Howard's policy iteration on deterministic discounted and average-reward Markov decision processes (MDPs), with a constant number of actions per state. This rules out strong polynomiality of Howard's policy iteration in both settings. We further prove that a Dantzig counterpart of Howard's policy iteration runs in strongly polynomial time on deterministic average-reward MDPs. Together with the known strongly polynomial bound for Dantzig's rule on deterministic discounted MDPs, these results establish an exponential separation between the two algorithms in both settings. This separation between Howard's decentralized and simultaneous selfish improvements and Dantzig's coordinated selection of a single action with the largest improvement across all states reveals a ``price'' of algorithmic anarchy.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: Added results on average-reward MDPs and extended the discounted lower bounds to constant-bit integer rewards

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Selecting the 7th Smallest of 16 Elements Takes Exactly 28 Comparisons
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Let $V_i(n)$ denote the minimum worst-case number of comparisons needed to find the $i$-th smallest of $n$ distinct elements. We construct algorithms showing $V_7(16)\le28$ and $V_8(16)\le29$, improving the previously reported upper bounds of 30 and 31. Together with known lower bounds, these results establish $V_7(16)=28$ and leave $V_8(16)\in\{28,29\}$. For 17 elements, we establish $V_5(17)=27$ and improve the upper bounds for ranks 6 through 9 to 29, 30, 31, and 31, respectively. Every new upper bound has an explicit decision-graph certificate verified by a static checker developed independently of the search. We also derive a lower bound for selection from a partially ordered state by combining the Fussenegger-Gabow weight with its order-reversed counterpart. All new upper bounds and this lower bound are formally verified in Lean 4. For $V_8(16)$, we show that a lower bound based solely on the total number of decision-tree leaves cannot establish $V_8(16)\ge29$. The algorithms were found using fixed-budget search, information-guided comparison ordering, and proof-number search. Proof-number search was decisive in finding the 28-comparison algorithm; in our experiments, refuting a comparison budget remained substantially more expensive than finding an algorithm within it.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 11 pages, 1 figure, 4 tables. Code, certificates and Lean proofs: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23346948

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Optimal Support Size Testing
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We present an optimal tester for support size that determines whether an unknown probability distribution is supported on $n$ elements or $\varepsilon$-far away (in total variation distance) with sample complexity $Θ(\frac{n}{\varepsilon\log(n)})$, improving the prior best $O(\frac{n}{\varepsilon\log(n)} \log(\min\{\frac{1}{\varepsilon}, n\}))$ due to Ferreira Pinto Jr. and Harms (STOC 2025). As a generalization, we provide a pretty good lower bound on support size.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Exploring Minimal Blocking Sets for Kernelization Lower Bounds for $\mathcal{F}$-Minor Deletion
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
For Vertex Cover, a minimal blocking set of a graph $G$ is an inclusion-wise minimal vertex set contained in no minimum vertex cover of $G$. Bougeret et al. [SIDMA 2022] showed that, for all minor-closed graph classes $\mathcal{G}$, Vertex Cover has a polynomial kernel parameterized by the distance to $\mathcal{G}$ if and only if $\mathcal{G}$ has bounded minimal blocking sets.
  In this work, we explore how far this connection between minimal blocking sets and kernelization extends to $\mathcal{F}$-Minor Deletion parameterized by the deletion distance to $\mathcal{G}$. A minimal $\mathcal{F}$-blocking set of $G$ is a minimal vertex set not contained in any optimal $\mathcal{F}$-Minor Deletion solution of $G$. For connected families $\mathcal{F}$, we show that if some graph class $\mathcal{G}$ closed under disjoint union has unbounded minimal $\mathcal{F}$-blocking sets, then $\mathcal{F}$-Minor Deletion parameterized by the deletion distance to $\mathcal{G}$ has no polynomial kernel. This generalizes a result of Hols et al. [SIDMA 2022] for Vertex Cover. We then show that this criterion does not capture all kernelization lower bounds for $\mathcal{F}$-Minor Deletion, even for minor-closed graph classes. Motivated by the work of Dekker and Jansen [Discrete Appl. Math. 2024], we study the more general notion of extended $\mathcal{F}$-blocking sets and the kernelization lower bounds they yield.
  For every fixed integer $η\geq 1$, Pw-$η$ Deletion is the problem of deleting at most $k$ vertices to reduce the pathwidth to at most $η$. We show that it has no polynomial kernel parameterized by the distance to graphs with pathwidth at most $η+1$. Moreover, for connected families $\mathcal{F}$, we show that $\mathcal{F}$-Minor Deletion parameterized by the distance to graphs with pathwidth at most $\max_{F\in\mathcal{F}} pw(F)+1$ has no polynomial kernel.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: Full version of an IPEC 2026 contribution. Abstract has been shortened for arXiv

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Semi-Streaming Estimation of the Held--Karp Bound and Graph-Metric TSP Cost
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
The Held--Karp bound is a linear-programming lower bound for the metric traveling salesperson problem (TSP). We approximate this bound in the multi-pass insertion-only streaming model for metrics induced by connected positive-weight graphs. For an $n$-vertex, $m$-edge graph and $0<\eps\le1/2$, the algorithm returns a $(1+\eps)$ upper approximation with high probability, using $\wtO(\eps^{-4})$ passes, $\wtO(n\eps^{-2})$ words, and $\wtO(m\eps^{-4})$ arithmetic operations per pass.
  We replace the changing edge-weight vector by a short history of multiplicative-weights (MWU) updates. After initialization, updates repeat until a column is removed. We store each repeated update once, with its repetition count. The record length depends on the number of columns, not updates; the argument applies to any fixed nonnegative matrix. For Held--Karp, tree-path queries recover edge weights from these records. Separate search and update thresholds allow fresh sparsifiers at successive search stages. Controlled rounding gives a bounded-precision implementation.
  The estimate yields a $(3/2+\eps)$ graph-metric TSP value estimate and a $(7/5+\eps)$ estimate when the input graph is unweighted. Conversely, in weighted graph streams, every one-pass $(1+η)$ upper approximation to Held--Karp, for fixed $0\leη<1$, requires quadratic space. The algorithms estimate values; they do not construct tours within these bounds.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Sublinear-Time and Semi-Streaming Algorithms for Path Cover and TSP
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We give improved sublinear-time and semi-streaming approximation algorithms for maximum path cover, $(1,2)$-TSP, and Max-TSP. For each fixed $\eps>0$, our distance-query algorithm estimates the optimum cost of an $n$-vertex $(1,2)$-TSP instance from above within factor $2-\cstar+\eps=1.413184\ldots+\eps$, with high probability, in $n^{2-Ω_\eps(1)}$ time, where $\cstar=2(\sec1-\tan1)$. This improves the $3/2+\eps$ factor of direct matching estimation in this subquadratic regime~\cite{BhattacharyaKissSaranurak2023} and of the faster near-linear estimator~\cite{BehnezhadEtAl2024}. A single random vertex order defines an implicit bipartite graph whose matchings project to path covers. An alternating-permutation analysis shows that its expected maximum matching size is at least $\cstar$ times the optimum path-cover size. On long paths, even the best of polynomially many uniform orders retains only a $\cstar+o(1)$ fraction with high probability.
  In semi-streaming, we construct deterministic $(5/7-\eps)$-approximate unweighted path covers and $(9/7+\eps+5/(7n))$-approximate $(1,2)$-TSP tours, improving the respective $2/3-\eps$ and $4/3+\eps+1/n$ guarantees in~\cite{AlipourFarokhnejadMoemke2025}. For nonnegative weights, we obtain $2/3-\eps$ for path cover and Max-TSP, improving the earlier asymptotic $7/12-\eps$ Max-TSP bound. These algorithms use $\poly(1/\eps)$ passes independent of $n$ and $O(n\log(n/\eps)\poly(1/\eps))$ words. We compute two approximate matchings separated by edge deletion. A cycle-compensation lemma accounts for the weight removed when breaking their cycles. For unweighted graphs, a third approximate matching on a simple auxiliary graph with at most $2n$ vertices chooses component connections; a Tutte--Berge count proves the stronger bound.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: A Randomized Approximation Algorithm for Doubly Free-Boundary Macdonald Processes
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We construct an approximate sampler for finite doubly free-boundary Macdonald rail-yard processes with Macdonald, boundary, and edge parameters in $(0,1)$. The construction allows arbitrary finite sequences of additions and removals of horizontal or vertical strips and all four boundary types. It reverses a finite commutation--reflection history from a partition sequence whose entries are equal, with the common partition weighted by both boundaries. We derive local reconstruction kernels from the skew Cauchy, Littlewood, and branching identities. Bulk and boundary updates combine integer increments with conditional shape sampling at a prescribed size; same-sign swaps use finite conditional resampling.
  For $K$ reflection periods and an initial partition-size cutoff $M$, the algorithm terminates almost surely and samples the resulting approximating law exactly. We prove total variation convergence to the target process as $K,M\to\infty$ and give explicit bounds for both truncation errors, decaying geometrically in the cutoffs for fixed input parameters. Under fixed parameter bounds, we also bound the expected operation count of direct enumeration in a unit-cost model.
  We further construct an exact rejection sampler for the initial partition law without a size cutoff or evaluation of its normalizing constant. Using this sampler removes the size-truncation error, leaving only the error from the finite reflection history.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Subgaussian Vector Balancing by an Ising Model
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We show that the guaranties of the Gram-Schmidt Walk Algorithm of Bansal, Dadush, Garg, and Lovett can be achieved by an Ising model. Given vectors $v_1, \ldots, v_n$ of norm less than 1, we give a closed form for a centrally symmetric distribution on a vector $σ\in \{\pm 1 \}^n$ so that the signed sum $\sum_j σ(j) v_j$ is $1$-subgaussian. We show that the Glauber dynamics for this model mix rapidly provided that the norms of the input vectors are bounded below 1 by an inverse-polynomial.
  The proofs employ the theory of Lorentzian polynomials, and we use these techniques to show fast mixing bounds for other spin systems.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Adding an Edge in a $P_4$-sparse Graph
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
For a graph family~${\cal F}$, the minimum ${\cal F}$-completion problem asks for the minimum number of non-edges to be added to a given graph~$G$ so that the resulting graph belongs to the family~${\cal F}$. This problem is NP-complete for many subclasses of perfect graphs, while polynomial solutions are available for minimal completion sets or restricted input.
  We study the minimum $P_4$-sparse completion problem that arises after adding a prescribed non-edge to a \(P_4\)-sparse graph \(G\), with the resulting graph required to remain \(P_4\)-sparse. For the case in which $G$ consists of two connected components, each containing one endpoint of the added non-edge, we characterize the possible forms of an optimal solution. Combining this characterization with the solution of the other cases identified by the structural decomposition of \(P_4\)-sparse graphs, we obtain an algorithm for the general problem that runs in $O(n^2)$ time and $O(n)$ space.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Solving SAT via Treewidth Backdoors in Linear Time: Beyond Sparsity
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
The Boolean Satisfiability (SAT) problem is a remarkably expressive computational problem, serving both as a cornerstone of complexity theory and as a unifying language for a wide range of search and reasoning tasks. While $\mathrm{NP}$-complete in general, SAT is well known to be linear-time solvable on instances with bounded treewidth. This motivates the search for "hidden" tree-like structures in formulas---for instance by detecting so-called weak $t$-treewidth backdoors. Such backdoors are sets of $k$ variables that can be assigned in such a way that the remaining instance has treewidth at most $t$ and is satisfiable whenever the original instance is.
  Ever since Gaspers and Szeider [ICALP 2012] showed that finding a weak $t$-treewidth backdoor for a SAT formula is $\mathrm{W}[2]$-hard with respect to $k$, tractability results have been restricted to structurally sparse formulas---most notably, a linear-time algorithm for $d$-SAT (bounded clause-length SAT) by Fomin, Lokshtanov, Misra, Ramanujan, and Saurabh [SODA 2015] and a non-uniform polynomial-time algorithm when the incidence graph of the input formula belongs to a nowhere-dense graph class (or more generally is $K_{d,d}$-free) by Lokshtanov, Panolan, and Ramanujan [ICALP 2022].
  In this paper, we push the tractability boundaries of finding weak $t$-treewidth backdoors beyond sparsity and into the regime of "well-behaved" dense formulas. Aiming towards relaxing structural input restrictions from nowhere-dense to edge-stable graph classes, as featured in the theory of beyond sparsity for FO model checking, or to bounded VC-dimension set systems, we identify signed semi-ladder-freeness as the correct dense structural restriction that establishes the boundary between tractability and intractability along this line.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Stochastic Network Speed Scaling with Competitive Ratios Independent of the Network
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: In network speed scaling, jobs arrive over time at a network of servers whose speeds can be tuned, every job must be processed by the servers along one of its allowed routes, and the goal is to minimize the total flow time plus the total energy. For stochastic arrivals, the competitive ratio of Vaze and Nair depends on the network, through the lengths of the routes it uses.
